name: httpp
workload: Single-threaded repeated parse of picohttpparser's own classic sample GET request (image request with UA/cookie headers), 10,000,000 iterations x 5 runs, averaged.
claimed_speedup: At -O3: httppv2 (2.0.0) 8,893,776.12 req/s vs picohttpparser 3,939,350.39 req/s (~2.26x faster); httppv1 (1.0.0) 2,855,841.74 req/s, actually slower than pico at -O3. At -O0: httppv1 2,008,030.68 req/s and httppv2 3,475,424.44 req/s both beat picohttpparser's 1,130,465.28 req/s.
hardware: Ryzen 7, ~4.79GHz peak frequency (exact SKU not given)
tradeoffs: Header-only C, fixed-size stack-allocated header array, no SIMD (wins via lower per-call overhead, not vectorization). Only the v2.0.0 variant beats picohttpparser at -O3; v1.0.0 is slower at -O3 despite winning at -O0.
caveats: CPU stated only as family ('Ryzen 7'), not exact model/SKU, so capped below tier A. Benchmark request text is adapted directly from picohttpparser's own README example. Very new, single-maintainer, low-star project.
found_via: GitHub: gh search code "picohttpparser" "benchmark" -> cebem1nt/httpp benchmarks/bench-pico.c

name: hparse
workload: poop benchmark (like hyperfine, with hardware counters) repeatedly running standalone parse binaries for picohttpparser, httparse (Rust), and hparse (Zig) over an HTTP/1.1 request; measures wall time, CPU cycles, instructions retired, cache references/misses, branch misses.
claimed_speedup: hparse: 1.27s wall-time / 5.38G cpu_cycles / 8.01G instructions vs picohttpparser: 1.45s wall-time / 6.16G cpu_cycles / 34.7G instructions (~12.5% faster wall-clock, ~12.6% fewer cycles, ~77% fewer instructions retired); also beats httparse (Rust) at 1.54s wall-time / 6.53G cycles.
compiler_and_flags: zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast (hparse); cargo build --release (httparse); picohttpparser built via its own upstream Makefile with default flags (bench/Makefile)
tradeoffs: Zig-only public API (needs a C shim for direct C++ linkage); streaming/never-allocates design explicitly modeled after picohttpparser so it can be 'swapped in smoothly'. A separate skylake-tuned build target exists (-Dcpu=skylake) but its numbers are not published.
caveats: No CPU model or OS/kernel stated for the benchmark host, so methodology is partial despite public benchmark code and stated compiler flags -> capped at tier C, not A/B. Single-host, unspecified-hardware numbers.
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos --topic http-parser --sort stars -> nikneym/hparse

name: picohttpparser-rs
workload: Interleaved same-session microbenchmark (scripts/bench_compare.sh / bench_compare.c) timing a safe-Rust reimplementation vs the pinned C picohttpparser (commit f4d94b48) across 8 workload categories: tiny, typical (~400B), large headers (~4.9KB), response (~150B), chunked decode, malformed input, streaming (8 staged prefixes), and an 'upstream marker' (~620B, 11 headers) request.
claimed_speedup: Rust/C time ratio per category: large headers 0.680 (Rust ~32% faster), upstream marker (~620B/11 headers) 0.827 (Rust ~17% faster, flagged 'stability: CHECK'); but streaming 1.023 (near parity), typical 1.100, response 1.185, chunked 1.199, tiny 1.482, malformed 1.811 (all losses for Rust). Author also states native C with -march=native/pcmpestri beats scalar Rust by 1.45x, and -O3 regresses the Rust malformed-path result by 1.68x vs -O2.
compiler_and_flags: C oracle: gcc, default anchor flag -O2 (override via C_OPT env var, e.g. -O3 for labeled side runs); Rust: cargo build --release (rustc 1.96.1)
hardware: Intel Core i5-12400F, single machine, no CPU pinning, whole-loop timer (no p50/p95/p99)
tradeoffs: Rust only wins on 2 of 8 published workloads (large headers, upstream marker); it loses on the other 6, including a 1.8x fixed-cost floor on malformed/reject-fast input. No SIMD path yet ('SIMD prize' explicitly parked/unimplemented), so it cannot match C built with -march=native + PCMPESTRI. Real-consumer integration (H2O/Plack/Furl) is parked, not done.
caveats: Single machine, no CPU pinning, whole-loop timer, explicitly 'not portable' numbers per the author. Extremely new (2 stars, days old at capture time). Most workloads are losses for Rust; only cited here because 2 of the 8 published rows are genuine wins over the named baseline, which the README itself highlights alongside the losses.
found_via: GitHub: gh search repos "picohttpparser" --sort updated -> logicpl4gue/picohttpparser-rs

name: picohttpparser AVX2 fork (vkrasnov)
workload: Single-threaded req/s over two request corpora: pico's own bench.c request and fukamachi/fast-http's benchmark request (fukamachi.c), comparing the original PCMPESTRI (SSE4.2) token-matching path against a new AVX2+BMI2 bitmask path processing 128 bytes at a time.
hardware: Intel Haswell i5-4278U, turbo disabled for consistency
license: MIT OR Artistic-1.0-Perl (dual-licensed, inherited unchanged from upstream h2o/picohttpparser)
stars_or_usage: 20 stars (fork); submitted as h2o/picohttpparser PR #10, left open/unmerged until closed 2020-07-17
tradeoffs: Requires AVX2+BMI2 (Haswell or newer), so it is not a drop-in for older or non-x86 hardware; upstream maintainer never merged it, so it only exists as an unmerged fork/branch; requires 128-byte-aligned buffer handling per the design change from latency- to throughput-oriented processing.
caveats: Benchmark is from 2014 (gcc 4.9.2, Haswell laptop CPU) so absolute numbers are over a decade old, though methodology (CPU model, compiler, flags, public code) is fully specified, meeting tier A. PR was never merged into h2o/picohttpparser and the fork has had no commits since 2014.
found_via: HN Algolia: query "picohttpparser" -> Cloudflare blog "Improving PicoHTTPParser further with AVX2" -> h2o/picohttpparser PR #10 -> vkrasnov/picohttpparser (avx2 branch)
